correctness.rationale: Order comparisons X0/X1/X2 give five intervals with boundaries a=c/(2−c), b=c/[1+c(1−c)], u=1/(2−c), v=1/[1+c(1−c)]. Every permitted one-step atom arrow is a union of affine full inverse branches covering its entire destination atom; C→E has exactly two branches and all other arrows one. Composition therefore pushes conditional Lebesgue measure to the uniform law on any terminal atom for any finite past, establishing a genuine Markov chain, not a two-point surrogate. Its computed P_c and interval-length π_c are stochastic/stationary; direct characteristic polynomials give z(z−1)(z+1−c)(z²+c(1−c)) and adjacency z(z+1)(z³−2z²+z−1). Shannon branch cancellation isolates the sole double edge of mass c(1−c)/s, yielding exact entropy H_b(c)/s and fraction loss c(1−c)/s. Independent symbolic matrices and exact inverse-image triple-cylinder checks at four rational c verified the constants; the all-history proof uses the affine inverse-branch geometry.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks confirm only the sampled sizes and parameter instances; the theorem must rest on the inspected all-parameter proof.
